profile.headline: Sr. Manager, Principal Software Engineer at Genesys

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description: My work at Mesh++ spans all aspects of the development process, including management of the software development team spanning the globe, debugging device firmware issues, design of network protocols and software architecture, testing, QA, and even some IT work.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
While at Genesys, I was directly involved in multiple teams and projects focusing on high performance code and good design. I'll talk briefly about three projects that I was involved in.

1) Upgraded a multi-million LOC C++ codebase from VS2010 to VS2015, which included several deep changes to a custom implementation of the standard library. This work resulted in drastic increases in programmer productivity, caught several multi-year old bugs, and paved the way to several years of future side-work by myself to implement numerous portions of the C++11 type traits library from the standard library. I was able to gain a very deep understanding of C++ metaprogramming from this project and the work I did on the type traits code after.

2) Rewrote Genesys's custom C++ build system, to enable future work on distributed C++ builds to multiple computers simultaneously. My work on this taught me deep insights into parallel execution of discrete tasks, dependency graph management, large scale compile jobs and compile farms, and C++ best practices. This work also included building and deploying new tools to help other developers analyze their work against best practices. When I departed Genesys, I measured up to a 20% reduction in build times for the so-far completed changes, with several more planned. Build times at Genesys were measured in days, sometimes taking as long as a week. 20% might mean saving an entire day.

3) Implemented RFC 5245 (ICE). This code lives inside of a high performance media framework, which can achieve high numbers of simultaneous transactions and near-perfect CPU scaling. Working with this framework required numerous coding constraints to achieve high performance, as well as working with a geographically dispersed team and multiple different technologies. My work was plugged into a larger framework that implemented the WebRTC protocol, which powers live Audio and Video conferences. My code powers several million audio/video calls per week, globally.

positions.title: Chief Technical Officer and Co-Founder
positions.description:
Aerosta, LLC. believes that computers are revolutionary devices that have the power to vastly improve peoples' lives. We personally enjoy and strive for the piece of mind of efficiency and optimization. Out of that optimization, flexibility naturally follows. Aerosta is dedicated to maximizing the efficency and flexibility of one incredibly important aspect of the computer revolution, personal data storage. Our main product offers a highly scalable, redundant, and distributed network attached storage system intended for use in a home or a small/medium business. 

As co-founder and CTO, my responsibilities include everything involved in running a company, but focusing on the technology implementation, while my co-founder focuses his efforts on revenue growth.

positions.title: Software Engineer and Partner
positions.description:
Our primary product is a niche social networking mobile app that:
- has been as high as 5th place in the “Paid Social” category of the Android Market
- has approximately 27,000 paid users and steady-state growth of 800+ new users/mo with a 4.4 star rating over 1,100 reviews
- leverages page scraping (via xpath) and/or JSON for content acquisition
- leverages Android timers for automatic download of new Activity Feed entries
- leverages Android contacts integration APIs for friend sync
- leverages Android Service framework for background photo uploads
- leverages Android intent filters to interface with misc. other parts of the OS (like opening the app instead of the website when a user clicks a link from elsewhere, or participating in the the “Share Via” framework)

My roll in this is primarily support, and programming assistance for my business partners, where we frequently collaborate on the architecture of the app, and run code dojo's to implement new features or fix high priority bugs. Initially, I hosted some of the software development infrastructure on my own machines, and then later assisted in migrating that infrastructure to hosted solutions.

An interesting aspect of this project is that we aren't endorsed by the website that our app accesses, let's say that they benignly ignore us. We find that the developers of that website frequently make changes that have unintended consequences for our app, and lots of the architectural challenges that we've addressed have been involved in reducing the amount of breakage that can happen through website changes.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
InTech Direct, INC. offers a wide range of solutions for printing and fulfilling orders for lots of gift cards and similar. Many of InTech Direct's customers are large brands that you probably do business with on a weekly basis, such as food, home improvement / hardware, and many others. 

My responsibilities at InTech Direct include:

An overhaul of the tools and applications used in business processes, including deploying a hypervisor, storage cluster, and applications and databases to run those tools such as Atlassian Jira and Atlassian Confluence. 

I'm building a re envisioning and construction from scratch of the internal manufacturing QA software that InTech uses to ensure it's customers get exactly what they ask for. The existing system has limited functionality, and was created with TCL/TK. The new version is being constructed with the Qt framework, and includes remote management features, advanced database interactions, and a slue of reconfigurability that InTech Direct's business processes have been hurting for for years.

I am also constructing a new security camera system from first principals based on the Linux GStreamer framework to allow InTech to monitor it's factory floor and building for security breaches and accidents that may risk life and limb. This new system is expected to, at launch, need about 100 GB per day of data storage, and will take advantage of the storage cluster that I'm deploying for it's storage needs.

I also mentor a software engineering intern, helping her create new internal applications for customer service, shipping, production scheduling, and invoicing, as well as provide project management guidance for several remote contractors to do various projects as the need arises.

But that's not all, I get new little fun projects from my co-workers every day. The collection of utilities that I've created or improved is growing constantly, and the time savings for the business as a whole is growing rapidly.

positions.title: Lead of Software Development and Partner
positions.description:
Eperture, LLC. was a mostly owned subsidiary of CyberMetrix, INC. with the vision of providing each to use touch screen appliances that could simplify the life of people who are considering moving into a nursing home. These appliances kept track of appointments, medication schedules, medical history, phone numbers and addresses, and other easy to forget information. Additionally, each machine could be easily controlled and remotely configured by a caregiver or family member. Further, later in the project, we added an additional requirement of being able to hold live video sessions between the touch screen device and a remote party on any webbrowser enabled device. 

I acted as the lead tech everything, from machine procurement, to running two teams of interns stationed in two different offices, to managing a team of subcontractors (at the same time as the interns) in a third office, to software requirements, specifications and architecture, to tech support. Additionally, I was involved in multiple investor meetings, and presented the fruits of our labors and the additional planning we'd undertaken to the participants in those meetings. 

My experience at Eperture, LLC. was concurrent with my experience at CyberMetrix INC., GoldenSpiral Software, LLC. , and the tail end of JAM Customs LLC, and I feel that being challenged to succeed in such fundamentally different industries simultaneously has really prepared me for success in any industry that I involve myself in.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Linux software development and support: including both graphical user interfaces and low level system utilities. Languages include C, C++, Java, bash, python, and various others. I changed languages, frameworks, and component-libraries on an hourly basis to provide solutions for my co-workers and our customers. Customers typically expected a turnaround time from initial complaint to solution deployment of less than 48 hours. 

Linux server administration: including managing the build servers, policing code quality, and building installer packages for in house software, and also open source utilities. 

Linux application development: I typically worked on 1 to 3 big applications at a time, in between my other rolls, and generally was the only engineer involved in these development projects unless I requested help from other resources to take advantage of their skill or knowledge of the application domain that was being addressed.

An example application would be a graphical stripchart (think heartbeat monitor) that displays data gathered from an engine being tested by our software. This program was written in C++, and replaces a previous implementation that was written in Java. We measurably decreased resource consumption of plotting the same live variables by over 50% (CPU, RAM, I/O). For this project, I was responsible for about 75% of the initial code. After delivery, I was the sole maintainer of the code, and further reduced resource usage while adding additional features, with the code base standing at 60 thousand lines of code as of March 2013.

Another project was a Test Runtime Control system which allowed for test procedures written by an engineer at a remote site to be deployed to a production test bay with a minimum of operator training or intervention. I elicited requirements from stakeholders, wrote the specification, and designed the system architecture. Final delivery of this product was made in February 2013 with much satisfaction from the customer.

positions.title: Chief Technical Officer and Co-Founder
positions.description:
JAM Customs was started with the goal of providing a pre-vetted manufacturing network and web based CAD software to consumers across the country. Our vision was that if you could design it, you could have it created for you on demand.

My partners and I founded this company because we saw an opportunity to change the world. We were college students at the time, and saw this as a challenge worth setting for ourselves. We continued pursuing JAM Customers, making strides on meeting industry contacts and slowly puzzling the pieces of our software together over the following several years.

In 2010 a change in market conditions brought on by a new competitor entering the market caused us to shift focus away from web based CAD software, to machining high grade steel hobby robotics parts, which we named Becreo. These parts are mechanically compatible with Lego and other leading brand hobby robotics kits. While we still make sales from this, it's no longer our primary focus, and we have moved on to bigger and much more world changing pursuits.

JAM Customs was a fantastic learning experience, and my team and I are proud of what we were able to accomplish on the budget of college students. JAM wasn't just a technical learning experience, but instead was the beginning of my career as an entrepreneur, which is something that I consider just as valuable.

My responsibilities included building and deploying our server infrastructure, conducting research into how to construct our web based CAD software, and any other technical activities that came our way. The educational value of launching a company, registering it, constructing a business plan, and deploying software services in a professional environment were absolutely immeasurable in value. I credit this experience as the foundations of my skills; building on my education.

positions.title: Software Development Intern
positions.description:
My assigned project at Forward Engineering, LLC. was to research, design, and implement a communications protocol for an Internet enabled Android based TV system for hospitals. This protocol needed to allow the unit to steam audio and video, read and send messages (similar to email), receive building wide emergency alerts, and allow for the unit to be remotely controlled by a central server.

Ultimately I proposed XMPP as the protocol of choice and had my proposal adopted by the rest of the team. From here, I designed a few extensions to the core XMPP protocol for our environment, and then implemented an appropriate plugin to the OpenFire xmpp server, and Smack XMPP library to implement those extensions. 

Additionally, my involvement in this project included implementing our Messaging client, and a daemon to act as an XMPP multiplexer / proxy.

positions.title: Software Development Intern
positions.description:
I worked on two projects sponsored by Trek, Inc. The first project had us implement a FTPS server to the Trek networking stack by combining the existing Trek FTP server with their existing SSL implementation. I served as a member of a team of three interns for around 4 months.

The second project saw me acting as team leader, with the team fluctuating over time from a size of one to a size of 3 interns plus myself. I was the primary client contact for the team, and responsible for setting the priorities of my team. During this project, we re-implemented the existing partial SNMP server in the Trek stack focusing on strict compliance with the standards (v1, v2 and v3), and adding missing features, while improving the API and implementing performance improvements across the board.

educations.fieldOfStudy: Triple Major in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Minor in Computational Science

My partners and I founded this company because we saw an opportunity to change the world. We were college students at the time, and saw this as a challenge worth setting for ourselves. We continued pursuing JAM Customers, making strides on meeting industry contacts and slowly puzzling the pieces of our software together over the following several years.

In 2010 a change in market conditions brought on by a new competitor entering the market caused us to shift focus away from web based CAD software, to machining high grade steel hobby robotics parts, which we named Becreo. These parts are mechanically compatible with Lego and other leading brand hobby robotics kits. While we still make sales from this, it's no longer our primary focus, and we have moved on to bigger and much more world changing pursuits.

JAM Customs was a fantastic learning experience, and my team and I are proud of what we were able to accomplish on the budget of college students. JAM wasn't just a technical learning experience, but instead was the beginning of my career as an entrepreneur, which is something that I consider just as valuable.

My responsibilities included building and deploying our server infrastructure, conducting research into how to construct our web based CAD software, and any other technical activities that came our way. The educational value of launching a company, registering it, constructing a business plan, and deploying software services in a professional environment were absolutely immeasurable in value. I credit this experience as the foundations of my skills; building on my education.

experience.title: Software Development Intern
experience.description:
My assigned project at Forward Engineering, LLC. was to research, design, and implement a communications protocol for an Internet enabled Android based TV system for hospitals. This protocol needed to allow the unit to steam audio and video, read and send messages (similar to email), receive building wide emergency alerts, and allow for the unit to be remotely controlled by a central server.

Ultimately I proposed XMPP as the protocol of choice and had my proposal adopted by the rest of the team. From here, I designed a few extensions to the core XMPP protocol for our environment, and then implemented an appropriate plugin to the OpenFire xmpp server, and Smack XMPP library to implement those extensions. 

Additionally, my involvement in this project included implementing our Messaging client, and a daemon to act as an XMPP multiplexer / proxy.

experience.title: Software Development Intern
experience.description:
I worked on two projects sponsored by Trek, Inc. The first project had us implement a FTPS server to the Trek networking stack by combining the existing Trek FTP server with their existing SSL implementation. I served as a member of a team of three interns for around 4 months.

The second project saw me acting as team leader, with the team fluctuating over time from a size of one to a size of 3 interns plus myself. I was the primary client contact for the team, and responsible for setting the priorities of my team. During this project, we re-implemented the existing partial SNMP server in the Trek stack focusing on strict compliance with the standards (v1, v2 and v3), and adding missing features, while improving the API and implementing performance improvements across the board.
